thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: inferpool-usw - node NotReady spike detected (3 nodes) — auto-paging #eng-oncall

alex: I'm oncall, looking now.

jamie: seeing the same, traffic spike + kubelet restarts on three gpu nodes.

alex: quick checks: `kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=infer-usw -o wide` shows 3 NotReady. kubelet logs show repeated restart loop. suspect kubelet watchdog on nodes a,b,c.

marta: also seeing a wave of pod evictions in namespace `inference`: `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Evicted` returns ~24 evicted pods, mostly on those nodes.

kevin: runtime logs from one pod show CUDA allocation failures and then OOMs before eviction:
```
E tensorflow: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
RuntimeError: CUDA OOM when allocating KV cache for seq len 2048
```

alex: okay, this is a mixed failure: node-level kubelet restart causing pod churn -> several serving containers hit device allocation errors as GPUs rebind -> OOMs/evictions.

jamie: mitigation plan: 1) cordon the 3 affected nodes 2) drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` 3) increase infer pool autoscaler by +2 immediately 4) temporarily steer traffic away from infer-usw with routing policy.

alex: executing step 1/2 now. `kubectl cordon infer-usw-node-12` -> done. starting drain on node-12.

incident-bot: NOTE: runbook referenced: /runbooks/inference/node-kubelet-restart.md (link)

marta: pushing route fallback in Redwood Console: set routing policy for infer-usw -> preferred fallback eu-west until pool healthy.

kevin: autoscaler scaled up new nodes (2) in ASG `infer-usw-prod-asg` — new nodes are Ready, kubelet stable so far.

jamie: I've restarted kubelet on node-13 via `ssh && sudo systemctl restart kubelet`, logs now show kubelet stable, no further crash loops for 3m.

alex: monitoring: error rate for inference requests in US-West spiked to 6% 503s for ~8 minutes, median latency for that region increased from 40ms -> 180ms during the incident window. Overall global traffic unaffected.

marta: customer impact: a small subset of customers using pinned dedicated capacity in infer-usw saw increased throttles and a few failed requests. No data exfiltration.

kevin: marking incident as mitigated — routing fallback + node replacement removed pressure. continuing to drain the remaining old nodes.

jamie: will open a short post-incident note and attach metrics (p50/p95/p99, error counts) and kubelet logs to the ticket.

alex: handing off to next oncall (marta) for 2hr watch. Please keep an eye on GPU allocation errors and autoscaler churn.

marta: ack, will monitor.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: inferpool-usw NotReady spike — mitigations applied; alert closed.

alex: thanks team :thumbsup:
